questions.a: It's a tool that sends guest feedback surveys by email, SMS or QR code, collects the responses and turns them into reports. Restaurant-focused platforms add location-level reporting, alerts for unhappy guests and links to your POS or reservation data. That helps you see whether a problem sits with one branch or runs across the whole group.

questions.q: What features should I look for in restaurant survey software?
questions.a: Look for multi-channel delivery that triggers surveys automatically after a visit or order. You'll also want reporting by location, real-time alerts when a guest leaves a low score, and integration with your POS and reservation system. Survey answers tied to real orders are far easier to act on than standalone responses.

questions.q: How do I get more guests to complete restaurant surveys?
questions.a: Keep the survey short and send it while the visit is still fresh, ideally by SMS or a QR code the guest can scan on the spot. Short flows with only a couple of questions remove friction, and less friction usually means more responses. Automatic triggers from visit or order data make sure you don't miss the chance to ask.

questions.q: Can I use a general survey tool like SurveyMonkey or Typeform for my restaurant?
questions.a: Yes, general form builders are a quick, low-cost way to start collecting structured guest feedback, especially for smaller groups. They usually lack POS integration, closed-loop alerting and location-level benchmarking, though. As you add locations, you may outgrow them or need to pair them with a separate analytics tool.

questions.q: What happens to negative feedback from a restaurant survey?
questions.a: A good platform alerts the right manager as soon as a low score arrives so they can reach out before the guest posts a public review. In Momos, negative responses go into an automated customer recovery workflow, while happy guests are invited to leave a Google review. That way each survey response leads to a next step.
